analysis.title: Market volatility reinforces case for portfolio resilience
key_insights: US equities fell again on Thursday. The S&P 500 closed down 2% and the Nasdaq Composite down 2.3%. The sell-off continued in Asia on Friday, with the Nikkei 225 down 4.5% and Taiwan's benchmark down 6.2% at the time of writing.

The decline was broad. All major S&P 500 sectors fell and decliners substantially outnumbered advancers on both the NYSE and Nasdaq. Recent selling follows pressure on chipmakers and cloud companies as investors question the scale of AI infrastructure investment.

Minutes of the Fed's October meeting indicated nearly all policymakers expected further tightening to be necessary if the US economy evolves as anticipated. Markets priced a near certainty of a 25bp hike in December.

Hunterbrook published a short-sell report on AMD (-7.7%) over fears its China business may be hit by stricter US chip restrictions. NVIDIA fell 3.3%, extending recent losses despite an upbeat revenue forecast earlier in the week.

UBS does not think the economic expansion, corporate earnings cycle or structural AI investment story has broken. The 2027 base case is near-trend growth, rising profits, more AI investment and moderating inflation later in the year.

UBS recently downgraded global equities from Attractive to Neutral, citing elevated expectations, high index concentration and a wider range of AI outcomes. The AI debate is shifting from whether investment continues to whether it can generate sufficient revenues and shareholder returns.

UBS estimates cumulative US tech AI infrastructure investment could approach USD 5tr by end-2028, and that AI model and application revenues would need to reach at least USD 1.5tr by 2030 for an adequate industry return. Competition, price cuts, costly monetization and open-weight models threaten returns.
UBS expects 25bp Fed hikes in December 2026 and March 2027 but no prolonged tightening cycle. Higher rates should weigh on consumer demand and base effects should moderate underlying inflation.

Equity positioning: UBS expects about 15% S&P 500 earnings growth in 2027. The top 10 companies are 39% of the index. The Eurozone is the preferred region (15% earnings growth forecast for 2027, lower valuation than the US). It favors industrials and health care, and suggests equal-weight US strategies to reduce tech concentration.

Within US tech, UBS favors financially strong hyperscalers with visible AI monetization and select leaders in compute, foundry, semiconductor equipment and infrastructure software. It is cautious on leveraged capacity providers, lower-quality suppliers and companies whose valuations depend on persistent bottlenecks or distant cash flows.

Fixed income: UBS favors intermediate duration (two to 10 years) and sees the best return opportunity in EM and high yield bonds. EM sovereign and corporate bonds yield about 7.1% and 7.0%, and US high yield about 8.3%.
Volatility: UBS advises using structured strategies to build exposure in a tailored way. Higher implied volatility raises their appeal, with diversification and careful sizing favored.

Gold fell 2.6% on Friday to below USD 3,530/oz, the lowest since September 2025, and is down nearly 9% week to date, on track for its biggest weekly decline since March. Drivers were stronger US labor data, above-consensus inflation and hawkish Fed comments on outsized hikes.

UBS thinks the market may be overestimating the level and duration of higher rates. It sees a long gold position as attractive, or selling volatility, and maintains a view that gold gravitates back toward USD 5,000/oz in late 2027.

Alibaba reported Q3 cloud revenue growth of 53% y/y, external cloud revenue up more than 60%, and cloud margin of about 14.5% versus below 10% two quarters earlier. It kept its USD 100bn cloud revenue ambition for 2030 and noted greater use of domestic processors. Tencent's cloud growth accelerated to around 35% y/y with a second straight quarter of negative free cash flow.
UBS favors China tech areas with earnings visibility and policy support, particularly onshore semiconductor equipment vendors, foundries and hardware makers benefiting from AI chip localization.

Australia's unemployment rose to 4.9% in October versus 4.7% expected, with 43,500 jobs lost versus a forecast gain of 25,000. AUDUSD was at 0.6650, its ninth straight daily decline, and has erased all its 2026 gain.

UBS downgraded the Australian dollar to Unattractive. The RBA has hiked five times this year to 4.85% (the highest in 18 years) and its latest hike vote was split 6-3. UBS sees USD strength fading from Q2 2027 and favors the British pound and select EM currencies.

NVIDIA fell 3.3%, extending recent losses despite an upbeat revenue forecast issued earlier in the week.
Alibaba reported Q3 cloud revenue growth of 53% y/y with cloud margin of about 14.5%, and kept its USD 100bn cloud revenue ambition for 2030.
Tencent said cloud growth accelerated to around 35% y/y, though higher capex led to a second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow.

sector_views.rationale: Favored sector in the Eurozone, where earnings drivers span manufacturing, defense, infrastructure and electrification.
Favors financially strong hyperscalers and select compute, foundry, semiconductor equipment and infrastructure software leaders. Cautious on leveraged capacity providers and lower-quality suppliers.
Favors onshore semiconductor equipment vendors, foundries and hardware companies benefiting from AI chip localization.
Downgraded from Attractive to Neutral on elevated expectations, index concentration and a wider range of AI outcomes.

earnings_insights: Alibaba reported Q3 cloud revenue growth of 53% y/y on Thursday, with external cloud revenue up more than 60% y/y. Cloud margin was roughly 14.5%, up from below 10% two quarters earlier.

Tencent said earlier this week that cloud growth accelerated to around 35% y/y. Higher capex contributed to a second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow, and management said spending was near a quarterly peak but could stay elevated for several more quarters.
UBS forecasts about 15% S&P 500 earnings growth in 2027 and 15% Eurozone earnings growth in 2027.

risk_factors: AI investment returns: competition, price cuts, costly monetization and open-weight models may threaten returns, along with financing, regulatory and company-specific risks.
Index concentration: the top 10 companies are 39% of the S&P 500.
Tighter monetary policy: further Fed hikes could weigh on consumer demand and add volatility.
Stricter US chip restrictions on China.
Australian housing market deterioration and rising unemployment.
vol_and_positioning: UBS advises investors to use volatility rather than fear it, with structured strategies to limit losses, generate income or allow measured market participation. Higher implied volatility, all else equal, may raise their appeal.
UBS sees an attractive risk-reward in a long gold position, or selling volatility to benefit from its positive gold price outlook, with gold technically oversold.
The top 10 companies account for 39% of the S&P 500, so small changes in expectations for a handful of AI-linked businesses can have an outsized effect on index returns.
geopolitical: Stricter US chip restrictions on China are cited as a risk to AMD's China business. Alibaba and Tencent said the latest US chip restrictions should not materially affect capex or cloud revenue, and both stressed growing reliance on domestic chips.
